meta.name: Triage and escalate support tickets with OpenAI, Google Sheets, and Gmail

name: Manage Support Tickets With AI Triage, Knowledge Base Matching, And SLA Escalations

parameters.content:
## Manage Support Tickets With AI Triage, Knowledge Base Matching, And SLA Escalations

### How it works

This workflow manages inbound support tickets by receiving them through a webhook, validating and redacting the payload, checking for duplicates, enriching with customer context, and matching relevant knowledge base articles. It sends the enriched ticket to OpenAI for classification, calculates SLA and escalation details, logs the ticket to Google Sheets, and either responds as logged or escalates to a human with an email notification. A separate scheduled path runs every morning to scan open tickets and email an SLA risk digest when needed.

### Setup steps

- Configure the webhook URL in the system that submits support tickets and confirm the expected ticket fields match the validation code.
- Connect Google Sheets credentials and set up the referenced sheets or tabs for open tickets, customer context, knowledge base articles, ticket logs, and escalation logs.
- Configure the OpenAI HTTP request with a valid API key, model, and request body for ticket classification.
- Connect Gmail credentials and set the escalation recipient list and SLA risk digest recipients.
- Review the schedule trigger timezone and run time, then test both the webhook ticket flow and the daily SLA digest flow.

### Customization

Adjust the redaction rules, duplicate detection logic, knowledge base matching criteria, OpenAI classification prompt, SLA thresholds, and escalation recipients to fit the support team's policies.

##  Receive and protect the ticket

The webhook receives a ticket from any support form or helpdesk.

The Code node validates required fields, creates a ticket ID when missing, and redacts emails, phone numbers, card-like values, and secret-like tokens before AI sees the content.

##  Enrich with support context

The workflow checks whether this customer already has an open ticket, looks up customer tier from the `Customers` tab, and finds related help articles from the `Knowledge Base` tab.

This gives the AI and the support team more context than a raw ticket alone.

## Classify and prepare SLA

OpenAI receives only redacted ticket content plus safe context.

The parser normalizes the AI result, calculates SLA deadlines, applies confidence thresholds, and decides whether human review is required.

##  Log and route the case

Every ticket is logged to the `Tickets` tab.

The workflow escalates duplicates, urgent tickets, security or billing risks, refund issues, VIP customer cases, and low-confidence AI classifications.

## Google Sheets setup

`Tickets`: Received At | Ticket ID | Customer Name | Customer Email | Customer Tier | Subject | Category | Sentiment | Urgency | Confidence | SLA Hours | SLA Due At | Summary | Suggested Reply | Related Article | Duplicate Open Ticket | Escalation Needed | Escalation Reason | Status

`Customers`: Email | Customer Name | Tier | Account Manager

`Knowledge Base`: Article ID | Title | Keywords | URL

`Escalation Log`: Logged At | Ticket ID | Customer Email | Urgency | Category | Reason | SLA Due At | Owner

parameters.content:
## Escalate to human

Creates an escalation log, sends an escalation email through Gmail, and returns an escalated response to the webhook caller.

## Confirm ticket logged

Returns the non-escalated webhook response when the ticket has been logged successfully.

## Evaluate SLA risk

Builds a digest of tickets at risk of breaching SLA and checks whether there is anything that needs notification.

## Send risk digest

Emails the daily SLA risk digest when the scheduled check finds at-risk tickets.
